title: Mock Hell (Over-Mocking / Isolated Fantasy Land)
pattern: A unit test where nearly all collaborator dependencies are replaced with mocks, fakes, or stubs, resulting in a large setup block specifying mock behavior and leaving zero or minimal actual production logic exercised.
why_bad: High coupling to unstable internal interactions rather than stable public API contracts [2, 8]. If the underlying implementation is refactored (e.g., changing logging or notification order), the test suite breaks even if user-visible behavior remains correct [3, 90]. It creates a "fantasy world" where tests pass successfully against obsolete mock assumptions while the application fails at runtime [107].
detection: A high ratio of mock expectation setups (`expect_*`, `returning`, `verify`) to actual execution and assertions. In Rust, this looks like multiple `mockall` or hand-written mock structs instantiated inside a single test.
fix: Re-architect the code to cleanly separate I/O from pure decision logic [15]. Test pure logic using plain values, and use medium/integration scope tests with real (or fake) implementations for the I/O layers [15, 19].
source:
*   *Composing Software*, "Mocking is a Code Smell" (p. 205-221) [2, 3, 5, 8]
*   *Practical Object-Oriented Design*, "Isolating the Object under Test" (p. 222-230) [90, 107]
*   *Software Engineering at Google*, "Test Doubles" (p. 257-280) [198, 204]
